name: Type Safety Checklist
description: This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any type safety task, implementation, or piece of work complete.
content:
This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any type safety task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Validate type safety outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
2. Document any non-obvious type safety decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
3. Measure before optimizing any type safety bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
4. Prefer explicit, readable type safety solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
5. When type safety guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
6. Surface known limitations of a chosen type safety approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
7. Prefer the simplest type safety approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
8. When multiple type safety strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
9. Re-check edge cases relevant to type safety (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
10. Check that type safety terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
11. Before starting type safety work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid introducing new type safety abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not skip documenting type safety assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of type safety correctness.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about type safety over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
